identity.title: ElasticMM: Efficient Multimodal LLMs Serving with Elastic Multimodal Parallelism

problem.claim: Efficiently serving multimodal large language models with heterogeneous requests and complex inference pipelines remains challenging because added modality components create inference overhead.

gap.claim: Existing tightly coupled serving architectures reportedly do not distinguish mixed request types or adapt parallelism across inference stages, resulting in higher time-to-first-token and poorer resource utilization.

contributions.claim: The authors introduce Elastic Multimodal Parallelism (EMP), which elastically adapts serving resources to heterogeneity across request types and inference stages.
They develop ElasticMM with modality-aware request separation and allocation, elastic partition scheduling, unified multimodal prefix caching, and non-blocking encoding.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize EMP as a new serving paradigm for elastic multimodal parallelism and present ElasticMM built around it.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On diverse real-world datasets, the authors report that ElasticMM reduces TTFT by up to 4.2× and delivers 3.2–4.5× higher throughput than stated-of-the-art serving systems while meeting SLOs.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLMs add modality-specific feature extractors and projection modules to handle images, video, and audio.
These components, complex pipelines, and heterogeneous workloads introduce inference overhead and expose limitations in tightly coupled serving.
The authors propose EMP and instantiate it in ElasticMM through modality-aware allocation, stage decoupling, elastic scheduling, caching, and non-blocking encoding.
Experiments are reported to show lower TTFT and higher throughput than SOTA systems under SLO constraints.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps distinct serving bottlenecks to corresponding mechanisms: request heterogeneity to modality-aware allocation, stage differences to elastic scheduling, and encoding or repeated-prefix costs to non-blocking encoding and prefix caching.

lessons.interpretation: This provides a concrete claim-to-mechanism structure that makes a systems proposal easier to evaluate.
lessons.application: When presenting a systems method, align each identified bottleneck with one named design component before reporting aggregate metrics.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when components interact inseparably or when the work does not support component-level attribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset identities, baselines, workload configurations, or whether the reported gains are overall or workload-specific.
No ablation or component-level evidence is reported, so the individual contribution of ElasticMM's mechanisms is unclear.
The abstract does not state which SLOs were enforced or the conditions behind the maximum and range of improvements.
